transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-21
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Mukherjee (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (StratusBridge VP Eng), Liang Zhou (StratusBridge Infra), Marta Ruiz (CTO), Aisha Khan (Partnerships)

Auto Summary (auto):
- Intro to StratusBridge's channel/reseller goals and expected GPU capacity for Q1 pilots.
- Discussed integration patterns (reseller, private VPCs), routing and quota models, and pilot scope: 2-week perf test using a quantized LLM on 4xA10s equivalent.
- Next: pricing deck, benchmark config, VPC access, deep-dive scheduled.

Topics (auto tags): partner onboarding, dedicated vs hosted, VPC & KMS, batching & kv cache, benchmark plan, margins/pricing

--- Transcript Body ---
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Priya from our infra team is here too. How's it going?
[00:08] Carlos Mendes: Good, thanks. Carlos here. We were excited to chat with you all about doing sort of a reseller and integration thing.
[00:14] Marta Ruiz: Hi, Marta. We're short on time but want to cover capacity and security gating.
[00:20] Priya Mukherjee: Awesome. Quick run the agenda: 1) understand StratusBridge GTM + technical constraints, 2) talk about expected GPU capacity and latency needs, 3) integration patterns (Reseller vs Dedicated private), 4) pilot plan and next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Liang Zhou: Yes, that works. A couple of items up front — data residency is a thing for some customers in EU, and we need to confirm KMS/HSM support and audit logs.
[00:42] Jordan Hayes: Totally — we can provide SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration. For Private deployments we do customer-managed KMS/HSM. Audit logs and exportable traces are included in Redwood Console.
[00:51] Aisha Khan: From partnerships, we're focused on margin tiers and onboarding time. We want to know how quickly we can resell capacity and what uplift is required for dedicated pools.
[00:59] Jordan Hayes: Understood. Typical flow is reseller agreement, then we provision a Dedicated pool or enable hosted with partner-marked routing. Pricing tiers differ if you want reserved capacity vs on-demand. I'll follow up with a reseller pricing matrix.
[01:12] Carlos Mendes: On the technical side, we're evaluating two routes: 1) Redwood Dedicated GPUs we resell to customers under our bundle, or 2) customers call Redwood Hosted via our routing token. Our ops team cares about control — e.g., VPC peering, private control plane.
[01:28] Priya Mukherjee: If control is critical, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is the path — it gives you control plane in your VPC and the ability to bring your own KMS. Dedicated works if you want isolated pools but still managed by Redwood.
[01:40] Liang Zhou: For benchmarks, our baseline is p99 latency < 250ms for 512-token prompts for chat endpoints, throughput ~ 200 req/s for embeddings, and cost target needs to be below X (we gave a ballpark in the pre-call doc).
[01:54] Priya Mukherjee: Sounds reasonable. Two notes: 1) latency numbers depend heavily on batch size and KV cache hit rate; 2) quantized model variants can reduce costs but sometimes affect tail latency.
[02:08] Carlos Mendes: Can you explain the KV cache behavior — we've seen references to "KV cash" in docs and want to make sure we understand prefix caching vs token-level cache.
[02:16] Priya Mukherjee: Sure — general idea is we keep the key/value attention cache to avoid re-computing for repeated prefixes. On a partner setup, automatic prefix caching and per-customer cache namespaces are supported. There's also an LRU TTL for cold-starts. Apologies if docs said KV cash — that's a transcription typo occasionally.
[02:32] Marta Ruiz: Does the caching require sticky routing to keep sessions on the same instance / pool?
[02:37] Priya Mukherjee: Good question. For best cache hit rates you want session affinity or support for sticky routing to the same GPU pool. Redwood's smart routing can prefer same-pool and fall back if capacity shifted. There's a tradeoff: strict stickiness can reduce global utilization.
[02:50] Liang Zhou: For our GTM we need the Smart routing logic spelled out — e.g., prefer lowest cost per token for background jobs, prefer lowest latency pool for interactive endpoints. Is that configurable?
[02:59] Jordan Hayes: Yes — routing policy is configurable by route and model. You can set latency SLOs, cost targets, and priority tiers; the runtime will attempt to honor them and fallback to compatible variants. We'll share the routing policy doc.
[03:12] Carlos Mendes: On the pilot we want to run a 2-week perf test with a quantized 7B-ish model across 4 GPUs. Can Redwood run that inside a StratusBridge VPC or do we need dedicated infra on your side?
[03:24] Priya Mukherjee: We can do both. For fastest results we usually run a dedicated benchmark on Redwood Dedicated in our infra and replicate the config in your VPC for the final validation. If you want private, we'll ship an installer for Private that you can run in your VPC.
[03:36] Marta Ruiz: Any constraints on model compilation and optimized kernels for quantized runs? We saw notes about compilation and kernel selection in the whitepaper.
[03:44] Priya Mukherjee: The runtime selects optimized kernels based on architecture and sequence length distribution. For int8/4 quantized paths we prefer certain kernels; some avx/arch combos change perf. We'll list recommended hw (A10, A100, H100 notes) and target kernel flags.
[03:57] Aisha Khan: What about observability and per-partner billing — do we get per-tenant dashboards?
[04:03] Jordan Hayes: Yes — Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-tenant dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and exportable CSVs for invoicing.
[04:10] Liang Zhou: Security review — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs? Also ok with SAML single sign on?
[04:17] Jordan Hayes: We have SOC2 Type II and are ISO-ready — can share certs. SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. For Private, you can enforce your identity provider.
[04:26] Carlos Mendes: Competitive Q — how do you compare vs NebulaCloud and Aurora where we already have some pilots?
[04:31] Jordan Hayes: Great question — high-level: Redwood focuses on deterministic production economics; we surface clear levers like batching, KV caching, quantization profiles, and routing policies. Nebula focuses on raw scale, Aurora on low-level infra. We'll share a short comparison doc.
[04:44] Marta Ruiz: Pricing — rough numbers are helpful, but for reseller we need margin structures and typical onboarding time.
[04:50] Jordan Hayes: Typical onboarding for a reseller is 2–4 weeks for initial enablement, assuming contract and access. Dedicated pool provisioning can take longer if it's Reserved capacity. I'll send the reseller matrix.
[04:58] Priya Mukherjee: For benchmarking, we'll recommend: 1) sample workload with 512-token prompts, 2) KV cache seed script to replicate conversation prefixes, 3) steady-state concurrency ramp test to check p50/p95/p99. We'll include a sample workload config in the benchmark bundle.
[05:14] Liang Zhou: Can Redwood's batching be tuned dynamically? We often have spiky traffic.
[05:18] Priya Mukherjee: Yes, the serving runtime supports continuous batching and adaptive batch sizing based on queueing and latency SLOs. You can set max batch windows and prefer latency or throughput.
[05:27] Carlos Mendes: For pilot success criteria we propose: average latency <= 180ms for 256 tokens, p99 <= 320ms, <= 20% deviation vs your baseline, and cost per 1k tokens below our target.
[05:40] Jordan Hayes: That seems measurable. We'll own the benchmark config and instrumentation so we can produce the traces.
[05:46] Aisha Khan: Commercially, what's the reseller margin?
[05:49] Jordan Hayes: Margin depends on commit level. I'll make sure the matrix shows 3 tiers with CCRs and discounts keyed to reserved commit.
[05:55] Marta Ruiz: A couple of nitty-gritty items: audit logs retention (we need 1 year), data residency options for EU customers, and whether audit logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[06:05] Priya Mukherjee: Audit log retention can be extended, and logs can be forwarded via secure syslog or S3 export; we'll include architecture notes.
[06:13] Liang Zhou: Are there any known perf regressions with seq lengths > 2k? Our embedding workloads sometimes hit long contexts.
[06:19] Priya Mukherjee: Long sequences impact KV cache and memory; kernel selection changes. For heavy long-context loads we recommend model sharding and appropriate hw sizing; we'll add that to the benchmark notes.
[06:30] Carlos Mendes: Ok, sounds good. Let's talk about timeline and immediate asks.
[06:34] Jordan Hayes: Proposed timeline: this week — pricing & security docs; next week — benchmark config; by 12/01 — VPC access and pilot start; week of 12/07 — deep-dive + live bench. If that works, we'll follow on calendar invite.
[06:47] Marta Ruiz: Works for us. I'll loop in procurement for reseller contract template.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: We'll also add product marketing folks to align on co-branded collateral after pilot.
[06:55] Jordan Hayes: Great. Any final questions or items we missed?
[07:00] Liang Zhou: One final: can Redwood support an on-prem air-gapped install for very regulated customers?
[07:05] Priya Mukherjee: Yes — Private on-prem installer exists, though it's a longer track with additional compliance gating. We can provide checklist.
[07:12] Carlos Mendes: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:15] Jordan Hayes: Thanks — we'll send notes.
